requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Where cases appear, they share the supplied rounded hard-shell construction: teal #356B70 base color, three raised vertical front ribs, two black lower-rear wheels, one fixed black top handle and a black side-seam zipper. Proportions and scale agree with 550 × 360 × 220 mm overall dimensions. Navy 60 × 45 mm handle tags carry centered ivory five-point star and circle symbols, with no other designed difference between cases. Perspective, lighting and natural occlusion are allowed; do not demand hidden wheels or numeric dimension labels in narrative images. Changed construction, implausible scale, added distinguishing colors or substituted ownership symbols fail.

Judge only depicted carriage geometry and station relationships. The interior should be compatible with the supplied 6000 × 2800 mm plan, centered 600 mm aisle, recorded paired seat-bank locations, forward-left rack at x 4800–5400 and y 0–1100 with a 450 mm shelf, adjacent pole at x 4500 and y 1000, and door-end openings at x 5400–6000. Camera placement remains compatible with the recorded interior aisle and right-side exterior camera areas. Platform left/right is measured facing travel, with Willow Quay and Orchard End on the right and Juniper Halt on the left. Perspective and partial views are allowed; visible spatial reversals or incompatible scale fail, while hidden geometry is not inferred as missing.

In narrative images, the mix-up reads as a mild comic misunderstanding, progressing through brief concern to shared relief. Hand actions, exchanged looks and tag details provide visible evidence of pickup, recognition or reconciliation appropriate to the depicted shot. Expression and staging may vary within that tone. Hostile, frightening or punitive treatment, or recognition conveyed without the requested visual performance cues across the relevant sequence, fails. Reference-sheet poses are not required to tell the entire story.

The two-page specification establishes the production facts as the initial planning basis: both character identities and clothing anchors, 1000/1200 mm heights, the recorded palette, six six-second shots, 36 seconds overall, acts at 0–12, 12–24 and 24–36 seconds, both exact dialogue lines with 22–24 and 32–35 second cues, and the 24–30 second interval reserved for audio description. Read the shot table and presentation for explicit repetition of shot count, runtime and all act intervals; the presentation also repeats #F3D9A4 and #B9CDD8 with their correct act assignments. Layout and wording may vary, but missing required facts or disagreement with the source records fails. Export chronology alone is not evidence of whether the specification served as the initial basis.

The character sheet shows front, side and back views and neutral, surprised and relieved expressions for each traveler, with readable 1000 mm and 1200 mm height labels and clothing colors matching the specification. Preserve the supplied upright-otter proportions, fur and cream muzzles, bare rounded paws, short tapered tails, Pip's mustard coat and anatomical left-elbow navy square patch, and Rowan's moss-green vest and round navy glasses. Compare all visible narrative appearances with this sheet. Pose, expression, lighting and framing may change; omitted sheet studies, inconsistent identity details or incorrect repeated heights fail.

Read six complete rows against 03-story-records.en.md: sizes WS, MS, MS, CU, WS, MS; successive six-second intervals from 0 to 36; both characters; and the recorded action, station and ownership in each shot. Cases are owned correctly in S01–S02, exchanged accidentally in S03 and still swapped through S05, then returned at 30–32 seconds. Both remain aboard at Juniper Halt. Pip says This one is yours. at 22–24 seconds; Rowan says Back where it belongs. at 32–35 seconds. The subtitle specification includes bottom-centered boxes of at most two lines and those two- and three-second durations. Equivalent tabular organization is allowed; omitted fields, altered dialogue, wrong timing or sequence contradictions fail.

Read the complete sequence and each act expansion against the fixed six-shot record. The journey runs Willow Quay, Juniper Halt, Orchard End; S03's pickup does not make either traveler leave the train. Possession follows the recorded correct, swapped and restored stages, with restoration at 30–32 seconds. Each landscape and portrait frame prints shot ID, its recorded WS/MS/CU size, parent duration of six seconds and character names. Act phases add increasing offsets within their parent shot and show successive actions rather than duplicates. Shared views retain Pip left and Rowan right. Tags remain readable, using detail insets when an oblique view obscures a symbol. Missing labels, contradictory phases or incorrect transfer order fail.

Apply this check to storyboard roles. The complete sheet has six 16:9–9:16 pairs; each act sheet has four pairs representing two successive phases for each of its two shots; each delivered performance sheet has three pairs within its designated shot. Every portrait composition rearranges framing and subjects to retain the corresponding action. Action stays within 3.5% insets and graphics within 5% insets measured from each panel edge. Simple crops that lose required action, mismatched shot pairs, incorrect pair counts or unsafe placements fail; different camera distance and subject arrangement are allowed when continuity remains clear.

Apply this check to storyboard roles and their relevant dialogue phases. S04 carries Pip's exact line This one is yours. with the 22–24 second cue; S06 carries Rowan's exact line Back where it belongs. with the 32–35 second cue. Both orientations place subtitle boxes bottom-center within graphics safety and use no more than two lines. Phases outside a dialogue interval may omit its subtitle, but each storyboard sequence covering the cue must represent it. The complete storyboard's closing panel prints THE NEXT STOP, with its 35–36 second appearance upper-centered inside graphics safety. Wrong speakers, altered wording, missing cues or unsafe boxes fail.

The color script explicitly identifies six frames in S01–S06 order, their positions on the 36-second timeline, three 12-second acts and both lighting codes repeated from the specification. S01–S02 and S05–S06 use warm #F3D9A4 lighting; S03–S04 use cool #B9CDD8 lighting. Narrative keyframes and storyboard phases agree with the script's shot-specific treatment while retaining recognizable local character and case colors. Normal rendering variation is allowed; incorrect code labels, reversed temperatures, missing timeline mappings or cross-file lighting contradictions fail.

The four images visibly establish their assigned events: Pip and Rowan with their owned cases at Willow Quay's rack; Pip taking circle and Rowan taking star at Juniper Halt; recognition through unfamiliar tags and a glance; and return of the cases at Orchard End. Composition may vary, but each assigned moment must be distinguishable through the characters, hands, luggage and setting. Repeated generic poses, wrong possession or an image depicting another shot fails.

Review the entire landscape animatic with playback timing. Its 12 seconds cover only S05–S06: the Orchard End meeting occupies 0–6, the exchange 6–8, Rowan's spoken line and exact subtitle Back where it belongs. occupy 8–11, and THE NEXT STOP appears at 11–12. Preserve the dialogue-free 0–6 interval reserved for audio description; this does not require silence from ambience or an added audio-description track. Compare the character, case, staging and warm-light treatment with the source images, preserving swapped possession until the exchange and owned cases afterward. Captions are bottom-centered, inside graphics safety and at most two lines; the title is upper-centered inside graphics safety. Wrong timing, premature restoration, missing speech or captions, identity drift or incompatible actions fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: Count at least eight pages. Page one states the exact project title, six shots and 36 seconds. The account identifies shot IDs that visibly demonstrate character anchors and correctly locates mistaken pickup in S03, recognition in S04 and return in S06. Its timing and lighting statements agree with the specification. Page arrangement and prose may vary; insufficient pages, missing opening facts or incorrect event-to-shot references fail. Visible reuse is judged separately.

The pages after the opening visibly reuse identifiable material from every listed source, covering all seven earlier deliverable categories, all four keyframes, all four storyboard sheets and frames from the animatic. Scaling, cropping and page rearrangement are allowed when source identity and the information being presented remain readable. Merely naming a deliverable, using unrelated replacement art or omitting any source fails.

All visible traveler appearances preserve the character sheet's identities and distinguishing clothing details. Finished keyframes and complete and expanded storyboard views agree on shot events, case construction, possession and visible spatial relationships. All narrative images follow the color script's lighting assignment for their parent shots.
